guarantees.claim: For each integer k from 0 to 31, output bit perm_data[k] is assigned the value of data[perm_sel[k]].
Output bits perm_data[RandWidth-1:32] (if RandWidth > 32) are not driven by any assignment within the function, leaving them undriven (X).
guarantees.cond: when parameter RandWidth is greater than 32.

assumptions.claim: The function assumes RandWidth >= 32 so that the loop index k (0..31) does not exceed the output bit range.
assumptions.risk: If RandWidth < 32, accessing perm_data[k] for k>=RandWidth is an out-of-bounds error; if RandWidth > 32, high bits remain undriven.

assumptions.claim: The perm_sel array must contain valid indices into data, i.e., for all k in 0..31, perm_sel[k] must be in range 0 to RandWidth-1.
assumptions.cond: always when the function is called.
assumptions.risk: If any perm_sel[k] is out-of-range, data[perm_sel[k]] yields X, corrupting the permuted output and potentially leaking secrets.

uncertain_points.claim: The hardcoded loop bound of 32 conflicts with parameterized RandWidth; if RandWidth != 32, the function's behavior is incorrect (out-of-range access or undriven high bits).
uncertain_points.cond: If RandWidth is set to any value other than 32.
uncertain_points.risk: Out-of-range access for low bits or undriven high bits could leak X values or cause functional failure in secret-key permutation.

uncertain_points.claim: The definition of rand_perm_t type is not visible; its width determines whether perm_sel has exactly 32 elements and if element values are constrained.
uncertain_points.cond: any call to perm_data with a perm_sel that does not match the assumed 32-element array with valid indices.
uncertain_points.risk: Undefined behavior if perm_sel has fewer than 32 elements or element bits exceed RandWidth.
